previous_replacements.act_1_bgm: Preserve the warm fantasy identity but make the cue more peaceful, pastoral, patient, and intimate.
previous_replacements.act_3_bgm: Reduce depressive/funereal character; add deliberate cavern echoes and controlled acoustic bass weight.
previous_replacements.act_3_boss: Reduce depressive/funereal character; add deliberate cavern echoes, controlled acoustic bass weight, and epic martial war energy.

replacements.act_1_bgm: There is too much going on; keep it lighthearted, simple, peaceful, and slower in BPM.
replacements.act_3_bgm: Make it more droning, with oppressive bass and more pressure.

post_processing.method: Rotate by four seconds; preserve an eight-second tail; crossfade its final four seconds into the original first four seconds; concatenate after the rotated middle; normalize; encode Ogg Vorbis.

per_track_preprocessing.act_3_bgm: ffmpeg bass=g=12:f=180:w=0.7 before the shared loop/loudness pipeline
per_track_preprocessing.act_3_boss: ffmpeg bass=g=7:f=180:w=0.7 before the shared loop/loudness pipeline

quality_evidence.speech_detection: Raw manus-speech-to-text JSON is retained under res://assets/music/evidence/transcriptions/; every selected source has zero segments and empty full_text, and the structural gate validates the file hash and source-duration linkage.
quality_evidence.source_retention: Selected generator outputs and the rejected short attempt are retained under res://assets/music/sources/ with a non-importable .mp3.source suffix.

deviations.record: The first Act I BGM source measured 162.403208 seconds, materially shorter than the 180-second request. It was regenerated once per the predeclared rule; the selected source measures 177.528125 seconds.

The generation tool accepted .wav output paths but wrote MP3-encoded 44.1 kHz stereo source bytes. The observed codec is recorded rather than mislabeled; shipping assets were decoded and deterministically converted to 48 kHz Ogg Vorbis.

The first Act III BGM regeneration measured 110.785250 seconds, below the predeclared 164-second minimum, and its sub-220 Hz level was also weaker than requested. It was rejected and regenerated once with explicit full-duration and continuous bass requirements; the selected source measures 167.575458 seconds.

The selected Act III generator sources had the requested acoustic low-register orchestration but did not independently exceed the predecessor's normalized low-band balance. A deterministic documented low shelf was applied before the shared loop/loudness pipeline: +4 dB at 180 Hz for Act III BGM and +3 dB at 180 Hz for Act III boss. Final sub-220 Hz mean levels are -21.1 and -21.3 dBFS respectively, versus predecessor values -22.1 and -24.7 dBFS after normalization.

The selected revision-3 Act III generator sources followed the requested acoustic low-register palette but, after common loop/loudness normalization, the first bounded shelves (+6 dB BGM, +5 dB boss at 180 Hz) did not both exceed revision-2 low-band measurements. Processing was not accepted. The smallest subsequent tested settings that cleared the predeclared stronger-bass criterion were +12 dB for BGM and +7 dB for boss at 180 Hz, recorded in catalog and provenance. Final sub-220 Hz means are -20.8 and -21.0 dBFS versus revision-2 -21.1 and -21.3 dBFS; spectral low-band shares increased 22.0% and 4.0%.

revision_analysis.method: External deterministic NumPy/ffmpeg comparison over revision-2 and revision-3 normalized shipping cues; metrics are objective proxies, not human judgments of mood or instrument identity.

act_1_bgm.interpretation: Lower spectral change, fewer onset proxies, and less upper-band activity support the requested simpler and less busy arrangement; peacefulness remains human-only.

act_3_bgm.interpretation: A larger, steadier low-band share and substantially raised low-band floor support the requested continuous oppressive drone; emotional pressure remains human-only.

act_3_boss.interpretation: More low-band weight than revision 2 plus greater transient and low-mid activity than the paired BGM support a heavier martial transformation; brass, taiko, and epic character remain human listening judgments.
